issue: The caption's capacity arithmetic omits the ~2.0 req/s per-host capacity, so one parenthetical contradicts the sentence it supports and another understates the fleet capacity by 2x.
evidence: Caption: 'so a 3-host fleet (3x0.9 req/s) is sized above it' - 3 x 0.9 = 2.7 req/s, which is below the 5.5 req/s burst the sentence claims it exceeds, and contradicts the figure's own 'one host ~2.0 req/s' and the orange N-1 residual line at 6.0 req/s. Later: 'at p = 0.85 it is 3 x 0.85 = 2.55 req/s' - the per-host 2.0 req/s factor is missing; the correct value is 3 x 2.0 x 0.85 = 5.1 req/s (still below 5.5, so the conclusion survives).
acceptance_test: Rewrite both parentheticals with the per-host factor included ('3 x 2.0 = 6.0 req/s at p = 1'; '3 x 2.0 x 0.85 = 5.1 req/s'); confirm every capacity number in the caption can be reproduced from the figure's own 2.0 req/s per-host bound.

figure: Figure 17.1 caption vs plotted N-1 residual line
issue: The caption's N-1 residual value conflicts with the figure's plotted residual line and with its own stated margin.
evidence: Caption: 'at ideal p = 1 the N-1 residual = 3 request (~6.6 req/s) clears ~5.5 req/s burst with ~0.5 req/s margin'. The figure's orange 'N = 1 residual (1 host drains, ideal)' line is at 6.0 req/s (3 hosts x 2.0), and 6.0 - 5.5 = 0.5 matches the stated margin, whereas 6.6 - 5.5 = 1.1 does not. '3 request' is also ungrammatical.
acceptance_test: Change the parenthetical to '~6.0 req/s' (or, if 6.6 is intended, redraw the residual line and restate the margin); fix '3 request' -> '3 requests'.

issue: Legend/plot mismatch: the legend lists two orange entries with different dash patterns, but the plot contains only one orange line and no line at 2.0 req/s, so the plotted dashed line matches the wrong legend sample.
evidence: Legend entries: 'offered load (burst)' (red solid), 'N = 4 fleet capacity (~8.0, ideal)' (blue solid), 'one host burst (~2.0, ideal)' (orange dashed), 'N = 1 residual (1 host drains, ideal)' (orange dotted). The plot contains a blue solid line at 8.0 and one orange dashed line at 6.0; there is no line at 2.0 req/s and no orange dotted line. The in-plot text 'one host cannot meet load above ~2.0 req/s' asserts a bound the figure never draws.
acceptance_test: Either draw the single-host 2.0 req/s reference line and keep both legend entries, or delete the 'one host burst' entry and make the residual line's dash pattern match its legend sample; confirm every legend sample maps to exactly one plotted line.

issue: The black label 'one host ~2.0 req/s' at the right of the plot lies on the descending red burst curve.
evidence: The label sits at roughly x = 8.5-10.5 h, y ~ 2.4 req/s; over that x-range the red curve falls from ~2.8 to ~2.2 req/s, so the curve stroke passes through the glyphs.
acceptance_test: Move the label clear of the curve (e.g. below the curve or with a short leader) and confirm in the rendered PDF that no curve stroke intersects the label glyphs.

issue: The annotation sentence is garbled: a subject token is missing, a dimensionless factor is written with a time unit, and one clause is not a sentence.
evidence: Box text: 'ideal p = 1 analytical ceiling - no SLO claim. N-1 clears the burst only for p ~ 0.917: req/s burst at p = 1.4h is the N-1 reserve so y still clear it after one host drains: N_provisioned = ...'. The subject ('the 5.5') is missing before 'req/s burst'; 'p = 1.4h' mixes a dimensionless factor with a duration (the burst peak is at t ~ 5.4 h on the x-axis); 'so y still clear it' is not a clause.
acceptance_test: Rewrite as: 'N-1 clears the burst only for p >= 0.917: the 5.5 req/s burst at t ~ 5.4 h is covered by the 3-host residual (6.0 req/s at p = 1)'; confirm every symbol in the box is defined and dimensionally consistent.

issue: Dangling clause in the caption: '...at p = 0.85 it is 3 x 0.85 = 2.55 req/s, so the 5.5 burst - so the 6.0 rps residual is not a robust failover margin...'.
evidence: The fragment 'so the 5.5 burst -' has no predicate and is followed by a second 'so', leaving the sentence without a main clause.
acceptance_test: Complete or delete the fragment; read the caption aloud for grammatical continuity after the FIG-310-04 rewrite.

issue: The color legend is incomplete and overloaded. It reads 'color: blue = specialist . teal = frontier . green = small gen . purple = general-purpose' but omits the amber fill used for the three decision nodes (Capability filter, Cost/SLO gate, Fallthrough), and the 'Request' box is filled with the same blue the legend assigns to 'specialist'. A reader applying the legend literally classifies the request as a specialist model.
evidence: Rendered page inspection: 'Request' and 'Embedding'/'Vision'/'Math-reason' share the same blue fill and white bold type; the legend's blue key is labelled 'specialist'. The amber fill of the three decision nodes has no key entry.
acceptance_test: The legend enumerates every fill class used in the figure (including the decision-node class and the request/source class), and no box's fill is ambiguous under the legend. Acceptance: a reader can classify all 10 boxes in the figure using the legend alone, with no class unassigned and no class assigned to two different meanings.

issue: White bold text on the amber decision-node fills (Capability filter, Cost/SLO gate, Fallthrough) is the weakest text in the figure once the page is printed in grayscale. The amber appears to be a mid-light orange (approximately #E8A33D), whose grayscale luminance is roughly 67%, giving white-on-amber a contrast ratio near 2.3:1 - below the 3:1 large-text threshold and far below 4.5:1. The three boxes that carry the entire routing logic become the least legible elements on the page.
evidence: Rendered page inspection: the three amber boxes carry white bold labels; the blue, teal and purple boxes are substantially darker in luminance and survive grayscale conversion. The amber class is also the one with no legend entry (FIG-18.1-02), so the reader cannot fall back on the legend to disambiguate.
acceptance_test: Convert the page to grayscale and measure the text/background contrast for every label in the figure; all labels must reach at least 4.5:1 (or 3:1 for bold >=14pt). Acceptance: either the amber fill is darkened to a luminance that supports white text, or the decision-node labels are set in a dark ink on the amber fill.

issue: The caption's evidence label mixes the book's two provenance/status axes: 'Assumption: status [ILLUSTRATIVE]'. Under the book's own convention (Ch 4 and the Appendix A axis table), [ILLUSTRATIVE] is a provenance label and [ASSUMPTION] is a status label; the caption places a provenance label in the status slot. The same book uses the correct two-label form for FIG 18.1 ('[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual] [DERIVED]'), so the figure-caption label syntax is also internally inconsistent.
evidence: Rendered page inspection: FIG 19.1 caption reads 'Assumption: status [ILLUSTRATIVE]'; FIG 18.1 caption (PDF 348 / printed 328) reads '[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual] [DERIVED]'; FIG 19.2 caption (PDF 363 / printed 343) reads '[DERIVED]'. Three different syntaxes for the same mechanism across three consecutive figure captions.
acceptance_test: All figure captions use one syntax: provenance label first, status label second, drawn from the book's defined sets. Acceptance: FIG 19.1's label reads '[ILLUSTRATIVE] [ASSUMPTION]' (or whichever pair is intended), and a grep of all figure captions returns a single consistent pattern.

issue: The cost/SLO gate's affirmative edge label is a four-line stack ('yes ->' / 'SLO:' / 'frontier' / 'cost: small') that mixes a branch condition with an unexplained rationale. The reader cannot tell whether 'frontier cost: small' is a condition the gate tests, a note about the frontier tier, or a restatement of the gate's name. The stack also sits in the same vertical band as the adjacent 'yes -> specialist family (one selected)' label, crowding the two branch annotations.
evidence: Rendered page inspection: the label occupies roughly four short lines immediately left of the gate's downward arrow, with the specialist-branch label ending only a few points to its left.
acceptance_test: The affirmative edge carries a single-line condition naming the selection rule (e.g. 'yes -> size tier: frontier if SLO requires, else small gen'), with any rationale moved to the caption. Acceptance: the label is one line, and the two 'yes' branch labels are separated by at least one line-height of clear space.

issue: The Fallthrough -> General edge is labeled 'no match -> general', but 'no match' has already been consumed by the capability filter's 'no' branch, which routes to the cost/SLO gate rather than to General. The same phrase therefore denotes two different conditions in one diagram, and the reader may conclude that a capability-filter miss bypasses the cost/SLO gate.
evidence: Rendered page inspection: the capability filter's outgoing edges are 'no' (-> Cost/SLO gate) and 'yes -> specialist family'; the Fallthrough -> General edge is the only place 'no match' appears.
acceptance_test: Each edge label names a distinct condition. Acceptance: the Fallthrough -> General edge reads e.g. 'no tier passed -> general', and no condition phrase appears on two edges with different meanings.

issue: Caption grammar error: 'Each specialist model (Embedding/Vision/Math) is a leaf of the router can dispatch to.' The relative clause is malformed.
evidence: Rendered page inspection of the caption block under FIGURE 18.1.
acceptance_test: Reads 'is a leaf the router can dispatch to' (or 'is one of the leaves the router can dispatch to').

issue: The caption applies the status label [DERIVED] to a figure that contains no derived quantity - no rates, no thresholds, no arithmetic. The caption itself defers the numbers ('the tiers, rates and thresholds themselves are in SS18.3.1-SS18.3.4'), so the status label has no referent in the figure.
evidence: Rendered page inspection: FIG 18.1 contains only box labels, edge labels and a color legend; no numeric value appears anywhere in the drawing.
acceptance_test: The caption's status label names the status of something the figure actually contains. Acceptance: either the status label is dropped (leaving the provenance label), or the caption states in one clause what is derived (e.g. 'the decision order is derived from the SS18.3.1-SS18.3.4 worked example').

issue: The caption's central distinction - 'a turn/to-kernel budget check - not the model's judgment - ends the loop at the limit' - is not visible in the drawing. 'limit hit' leaves the same 'Decide / check / resolved?' box as the model's own resolution, so the figure alone supports the reading the caption explicitly rejects (that the model decides to stop at the limit).
evidence: Rendered page inspection: the Decide box carries the sub-labels 'check' and 'resolved?', and two downward edges leave it ('resolved' to Final answer, 'limit hit' to Stopped) with no visual distinction between a model decision and a harness-enforced stop.
acceptance_test: The figure distinguishes the two checks. Acceptance: the limit edge is labeled to name its source (e.g. 'limit hit (harness budget exhausted)') or the Decide box is split into 'model resolved?' and 'budget exhausted?', so the caption's claim is readable from the drawing alone.

issue: The caption phrase 'a turn/to-kernel budget check' uses 'to-kernel', which is not a term defined or used anywhere else in the manuscript and reads as a typo for 'token'. A reader encountering it in a caption that is otherwise precise will stop to parse it.
evidence: Rendered page inspection of the FIGURE 19.1 caption; the book's established vocabulary is 'turn' and 'token' (e.g. 'turn-count distribution', 'tokens per request').
acceptance_test: The phrase reads 'a turn/token budget check' (or the intended term is defined in the glossary and used consistently).

issue: The small italic role labels inside the state boxes ('model', 'action', 'state', 'check' on the pale-blue row; 'emit', 'done', 'limit', 'terminal' on the amber row) are the smallest and faintest text in the figure. The blue-on-pale-blue role labels sit near a 4:1 grayscale contrast and the brown-on-amber role labels are lower still, so at print size the role annotations - which carry the state-machine semantics - are the first thing to disappear.
evidence: Rendered page inspection: the role labels are set in a lighter, italic face than the box titles and are visibly lower-contrast than the box titles in both panels of the figure.
acceptance_test: All in-box annotation text reaches at least 4.5:1 in grayscale at final print size. Acceptance: role labels are set in the same dark ink as the box titles (or in a dedicated dark accent), and remain legible in a grayscale print.

issue: Panel (a) has no x-axis title while panel (b) is titled 'Agent turns', even though the two panels share the same category axis ((single-shot), 1, 2, 3, 4). The reader must infer the shared axis from the tick labels alone.
evidence: Rendered page inspection: panel (b) carries the centered x-axis label 'Agent turns'; panel (a) has only the category tick labels.
acceptance_test: Either both panels carry 'Agent turns' or the figure uses a single shared x-axis label centered under the pair.

issue: Panel (a)'s y-axis tick labels are unseparated thousands ('2000', '4000', ... '14000'), inconsistent with the book's comma-separated thousands used everywhere else in the text and in the figure's own caption ('9,200', '12,960', '24.9 GB').
evidence: Rendered page inspection: panel (a) y-axis reads 0, 2000, 4000, 6000, 8000, 10000, 12000, 14000; the caption on the same page writes '9,200-token prompt' and '~24.9 GB'.
acceptance_test: Panel (a)'s ticks are formatted 2,000 / 4,000 / ... / 14,000, matching the book's number formatting.

page: PDF 363 / printed 343 (caption) and PDF 362 / printed 342 (adjacent prose)
issue: The caption and the adjacent prose give the reader two different numbers for the same effect and the prose's framing contradicts the caption. The caption says four turns take a request 'from ~24.9 GB KV to ~34.0 GB of KV - 36% jump'; the prose one page earlier says the same move 'is not a "35% GPU memory" tweak but a move from ~24.9 GB KV per request ... to ~34.0 GB KV per request'. The move the prose dismisses as a 35% tweak is the move the caption quantifies as 36%.
evidence: Independent recomputation: (33.955 - 24.890) / 24.890 = 36.4%, so the caption's 36% is correct on unrounded values; the prose's '35%' is the same quantity rounded differently and is used rhetorically to deny that the effect is small. The prose never states what the fleet-level amplification actually is, which is the point it appears to be making.
acceptance_test: The two numbers are reconciled in one voice. Acceptance: the prose states the per-request KV growth (36%) and then states the fleet-level amplification explicitly (e.g. the reduction in concurrent slots per host at fixed KV capacity), so the caption's '36% jump' and the prose's claim support each other rather than appearing to contradict.

issue: The caption sentence 'Caveat: a production stack that can hold this flat, prefix-cache reduces recomputation and shares prefix KV but does not by itself reduce the request's KV-resident context' uses 'hold this flat' without an antecedent the reader can resolve - flat context, flat memory, flat allocation? The sentence is doing real work (it is the figure's only caveat about production reality) and is currently opaque.
evidence: Rendered page inspection of the FIGURE 19.2 caption; 'flat' is not used elsewhere in the chapter in this sense.
acceptance_test: The caveat is rewritten so that 'flat' has an explicit referent (e.g. 'a production stack that can hold the accumulated context flat, i.e. without evicting or compacting it'), or the word is replaced with a precise one.
